chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Morris and Fry and the baseball gag
summary: Asked about black entertainment, he mentions the act Morris and Fry and recites a baseball routine placing the game's origin in the Garden of Eden.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: So in this few minutes, if you can do me a favor and just paint a picture of what black entertainment was
like in those days. What was happening in black entertainment, it certainly isn't like it is today.
No, there was no black entertainment much of yesterday.
Oh, there was Sissle and Blake around, there was lots of comics.
They were doing their show, they weren't around in vaudeville.
Were you involved with Sissle and Blake?
Oh, what's the name of that act I was going to tell you about before? It was Morris & Fry, that's what I was trying to tell you about the other day, Morris & Fry, "How high is up?"
If you brought a kid to the ball game and it's rainin', who's playin'. That's like the guy saying, "Who's on

first," See that guy doing that gag? "Who's on first?" But the baseball is the thing. You know where baseball was invented, dontcha? Huh? In the Garden of Eden. Eve stole first, Adam took second, St. Peter empired the game, Rebecca went to the world with the pitcher, while Ruth was in the field, won fame, (inaudible) was struck out by David base, a base hit was made by King and the prodigal son made a home run and Noah gave out checks for rain. That's how the ball game started.
What can I tell ya now? I can't think of a gag that's good enough.
